scenarios.name: Baseline
scenarios.description: No event in progress. Prices drift on their own volatility alone.
headlines: Trading opens quietly with no major surprises for investors.
Economists expect steady growth through the rest of the year.
Company earnings are broadly in line with what analysts forecast.

scenarios.name: Oil supply shock
scenarios.description: A pipeline outage cuts crude supply: energy producers rally, airlines and hauliers are hit.
headlines: A pipeline outage abroad has cut global crude supply overnight.
Petrol prices jump at the pump and airlines warn of higher fuel bills.
Energy producers rally while travel companies fall back.

scenarios.name: Surprise rate hike
scenarios.description: The central bank tightens harder than expected. A persistent repricing, not a passing scare.
headlines: The central bank raised borrowing costs by more than anyone expected.
Mortgage lenders move quickly to pass the increase on to customers.
Shares in banks climb while house builders slide.

scenarios.name: Credit crunch
scenarios.description: A large borrower fails to refinance and lending seizes up. The widest spreads decay slowest.
headlines: A large lender has failed to refinance its short-term debt.
Banks are charging each other far more to borrow overnight.
Investors are moving money into the safest assets they can find.

scenarios.name: Risk-on rally
scenarios.description: Inflation cools and buyers return. A broad, slowly fading advance led by growth names.
headlines: Inflation cooled faster than forecast for a third straight month.
Investors are buying shares again after a long cautious spell.
Growth companies lead the advance as confidence returns.

scenarios.name: Dollar surge
scenarios.description: The home currency reprices to a new, persistent level. Exporters and importers part company.
headlines: The American currency has climbed to its strongest level in years.
Exporters warn that overseas sales will be worth less at home.

scenarios.name: Recession scare
scenarios.description: Growth data disappoints across the board. Defensive names hold up, cyclicals do not.
headlines: Factory orders fell for a third month in a row.
Job vacancies are drying up across several large industries.
Investors are cutting back on riskier holdings and buying government bonds.
